ACCEPT-WITH-NOTES

## 1. What the lane claims

Lane 439 closes U4's honest energy slices and two exact energy identities, and U5's honest mixed paths and exact mixed scaling, over the canonical raw-field PlacementData. The statements reported at research/T15/REPORT_439.md:11, research/T15/REPORT_439.md:38 agree with the actual declarations. The five conformance checks are research/T15/probes/energy_mixed_closes.lean:54, :59, :66, :73, :81.

Read CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills/lane-review/SKILL.md, logs/LESSONS.md:1–40, the brief, research/T15/T15_SPLIT.md §0/U4/U5, the worker report and attempts, and reports 376/384/421. The requested research/T15/REPORT_333.md does not exist; a repository filename search found research/T17/REPORT_333.md, which concerns the T17 spec, not HaarBridge. I inspected HaarBridge itself. This is a brief provenance issue, not a missing lane deliverable.

## 2. What is in Lean

Paths abbreviated below: Energy/Mixed/Scaling/SingleCopy/HaarBridge mean formalization/NSFormalization/Section3/T15/{name}.lean; I03 means formalization/NSFormalization/Section4/I03.

| Field | Implementation | Canonical field | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| energySlices_memLp | Energy.lean:129 | Scaling.lean:341 | Exact velocity and full-gradient Haar L² guards for every t in (0,T), every admissible ε. |
| packetEnergyIdentity | Energy.lean:170 | Scaling.lean:352 | Exact ENNReal.ofReal (ε^(1/2) * M); M is the raw packet's least upper energy bound. |
| packetDissipationIdentity | Energy.lean:206 | Scaling.lean:363 | Exact ENNReal.ofReal (ε^(1/2) * D); D is the square root of the source dissipation integral. |
| mixed_memLp | Mixed.lean:317 | Scaling.lean:376 | Both genuine Bochner paths, all spatial/time exponents ≥1, including ∞. |
| packetMixedScaling | Mixed.lean:358 | Scaling.lean:390 | Exact factor ε^alphaT r q multiplying the unrescaled whole-space source norm. |

Paper fidelity: opened paper/sections/03-torus.tex:99–175 with sed. Lines 101–120 specify the fixed placement, ε>0, 2ε²<T, zero extensions and single-copy periodization; lines 125–132 state precisely these three norm equalities; lines 145–149 explain their scaling and endpoints. Spec.lean:790–850 uses packet projections; Scaling.lean:460–501 is the canonical raw-field replacement. No pressure/viscosity/PDE condition has been added to these purely analytic conclusions.

The Section 4 bundle is honest reuse: I03/Energy.lean:101 defines PacketData's eight clauses; Scaling.lean:466–483 supplies them; the compiled constructor at research/T15/probes/energy_mixed_closes.lean:96 establishes the conversion without additional premises. The explicit hu in the energy identities duplicates hP.support, but is satisfiable and imposes no new restriction. The field quantifiers are unchanged after passing these raw clauses. No newly named input or target-as-hypothesis occurs.

Opened and checked the reused theorems, rather than trusting their names: SingleCopy.lean:146 and :180 give the exact cube identities; HaarBridge.lean:154 and :216 give Haar/Lebesgue velocity/gradient norms; I03/Energy.lean:211, :304, :487 give the scaled slice and two time norms. Both energy time norms use Ioo 0 T, exactly T10/PeriodicData.lean:328 and :334, so no extra time-interval transport is needed. Mixed.lean:104 identifies the chart pushforward; :114 handles arbitrary exponents, not only 2. I03/Mixed.lean:140 is the positive-time scaling identity actually used at Mixed.lean:377. The binding equivalents were opened at verification/Bindings/Scaling.lean:296, :318, :658 and :667.

Non-vacuity: Scaling.lean:115 and :173 require T>0 and ε₀>0; :183 enforces the activation inequality. Norm finiteness is not silently replaced by top.toReal=0: Mixed.lean:164, :253, :262, :348 use explicit eLpNorm_lt_top proofs, and :326–353 constructs finite, strongly measurable Bochner paths. The unused q≥1 proof is harmless: these estimates are stronger than their canonical q≥1 interface. The definition of alphaT uses top.toReal only to implement the correct reciprocal endpoint exponent.

The concrete probe constructs a nonzero spatial/time bump with full PlacementData and PacketData (research/T15/probes/energy_mixed_closes.lean:120, :354), applies all five theorems at ε=1/2 (:372), proves M>0 (:401), and proves the force nonzero at source time 1/2 (:420). It compiled silently. This is a non-vacuity witness for the analytic hypotheses, not a claim that this bump is a full blowup/PDE packet.

Hygiene: 8 Energy declarations and 21 Mixed declarations, all 29 audited with exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. No admission, axiom declaration, native_decide, or heartbeat option in either module or the positive probe. The only keyword matches are explanatory comments at Energy.lean:42 and Mixed.lean:42. The comparison to origin/erenup/integration-section3 shows only new Lean modules/probes; the sole modified existing file is the permitted research status record T15_SPLIT.md. No verification file changed. experiments/build_changed_lean.py --dry-run explicitly lists both new modules, so the changed-module CI mechanism covers them.

## 3. Gaps and exact fixes

No mathematical or build gap remains in U4/U5. Findings are documentation-only:

1. **Minor, false boundary explanation.** research/T15/ATTEMPTS_U4_U5.md:22–24 and research/T15/T15_SPLIT.md:109 say the two gradients differ on the cube frontier. Under smoothness and strict interior support this is false: the source and its periodization vanish locally at the boundary, so both gradients vanish there. Single-copy equality alone is not a derivative theorem, which is the actual reason to supply regularity separately. Exact replacement sentence for D2: “The gradient guard is obtained from smoothness of the periodization; the value-level single-copy identity alone does not supply that regularity.” Exact one-line replacement at T15_SPLIT.md:109: “smooth — supplied by the vendor”. No proof edit needed.

2. **Minor, stale canonical citations.** research/T15/REPORT_439.md:56, research/T15/probes/energy_mixed_closes.lean:9 and research/T15/ATTEMPTS_U4_U5.md:5 cite 348,353,364 for the three U4 fields; their declaration starts are 341,352,363. Replace the five-field citation by “Scaling.lean:341,352,363,376,390” and the U4-only citation by “Scaling.lean:341,352,363”. Energy.lean:16 should cite “Scaling.lean:341,352,363” as well. Existing near-line references identify the intended formulas, but the first currently points to another field's documentation.

3. **Minor, stale probe description.** research/T15/probes/energy_mixed_closes.lean:21 and :370 describe three fields, while :372 proves all five. Replace “all three fields” by “all five fields” and the Part 2 closing heading/docstring by “The five U4/U5 fields on the explicit geometry at ε = 1/2.”

The report's “29 lines” (REPORT_439.md:102, ATTEMPTS_U4_U5.md:168) means 29 declarations; this run prints 37 physical lines because four entries wrap. All axiom lists are exactly correct. Prefer “29 declarations” as a wording cleanup; the semantic audit passes.

The report's out-of-unit gaps (REPORT_439.md:79–83) were checked by whole-Section4 grep, reproduced below. No Section4 PlacementData constructor or canonical mixedLebesgueENorm_eq/scaledForce declaration was found; the existing positiveMixedNorm_parabolicForce and both energy identities were found and opened. Placement construction for arbitrary packet data is not promised by U4/U5; the concrete instance is present. The binding duplication is explained by verification/lakefile.toml:6 requiring formalization, while formalization/lakefile.toml:5 depends only on the vendor package. No unresolved “not in the tree” assertion is used to excuse an unfinished U4/U5 field.

Negative check: research/T15/probes/rev439_energy_exponent.lean:20 copies the complete packetEnergyIdentity proof, changes only its name and the conclusion's exponent from 1/2 to 1, and retains every hypothesis/argument. Lean exits 1 at :28 with the residual equality of those different powers (exact output below). The original module is the passing control. This is a substantive main-statement mutation, not an argument-deletion test.
